g1.label: 1. Moshe’s parents ___ him go to Australia.
g1.why: "let" takes a bare infinitive (no "to"): let + object + go. The sentence has "him go", not "him to go".

g2.label: 2. They ___ him to go on the trip.
g2.why: "allow" takes a to-infinitive: allow + object + to go. The "to" in the sentence signals "allowed".

g3.label: 3. Moshe’s father ___ him read about the dangers.
g3.why: "make" means to force someone; it takes a bare infinitive like "let": made + him + read. The father insisted.

g4.label: 4. Moshe ___ his photo taken by a photographer.
g4.why: "have something done" uses have + object + past participle. Someone else took the photo for Moshe.

g5.label: 5. The hostel owner didn’t ___ them stay out after midnight.
g5.why: After "didn’t", "let" keeps its bare-infinitive pattern: didn’t let + them + stay.

g6.label: 6. The park ranger ___ the group walk only on marked trails.
g6.why: The ranger forced the group — "make" + object + bare infinitive. No "to" follows.

g7.label: 7. Cam’s parents ___ her to visit relatives in Melbourne.
g7.why: The "to visit" signals "allowed": allow + object + to-infinitive.

g8.label: 8. Mike ___ his surfboard waxed at the surf shop.
g8.why: "have something done": have + object + past participle. The surf shop did the waxing, not Mike.

g1.label: 1. When we arrived, the barbecue ___ by Mike’s dad.
g1.why: "When we arrived" sets a past moment; the action was in progress then → past progressive passive: was + being + prepared.

g2.label: 2. A new immigration museum ___ in Sydney right now.
g2.why: "Right now" means the action is in progress at this moment → present progressive passive: is + being + built.

g3.label: 3. While we were visiting, the refugees ___ by journalists.
g3.why: "While we were visiting" sets a past time frame; the interviewing was ongoing → past progressive passive: were + being + interviewed.

g4.label: 4. At this moment, traditional songs ___ at the festival.
g4.why: "At this moment" points to now; multiple songs (plural) are in progress → present progressive passive: are + being + performed.

g5.label: 5. When Bill bumped into the thief, the man ___ by a police officer.
g5.why: The chasing was already in progress when Bill bumped into him → past progressive passive: was + being + chased.

g6.label: 6. Don’t go to the Museum of Sydney yet — it ___ at the moment.
g6.why: "At the moment" means the renovation is happening now → present progressive passive: is + being + renovated.

g1.label: Jim ___ (warn) of the dangers before he left.
g1.why: Simple past passive: the warning happened before he left. was + past participle.

g2.label: He ___ (tell) that swimming in rock pools can be dangerous.
g2.why: Simple past passive: he received the information in the past. was + told.

g3.label: But he ___ (not attack).
g3.why: Simple past passive negative: was + not + past participle. Contracted: wasn’t attacked.

g4.label: We ___ (tell) so many stories about crocodile attacks.
g4.why: Simple past passive with plural subject "we": were + told.

g5.label: It now seems a wonder he ___ (not hurt).
g5.why: Simple past passive negative: wasn’t + past participle.

g6.label: More warning signs ___ (put up) soon.
g6.why: Future passive: will + be + past participle. The signs will be put up in the future.

g7.label: The kid who ___ (kill) by a croc just last week.
g7.why: Simple past passive: "last week" is a finished past time. was + killed.

g8.label: Let’s hope he ___ (find) very soon!
g8.why: Future passive after "hope": will + be + past participle.
